statements.statement: For fixed scalar measurable O with ||O||infinity<=1 in the same finite family, |E_eta O-E_0 O|<=|eta|.
statements.argument: Differentiate the normalized exponential family: derivative Cov_eta(O,z). Cauchy–Schwarz bounds its magnitude by sqrt(Var_eta(O) Var_eta(z))<=1, since |O| and |z| are bounded by1. Integrate along the real eta segment. For complex O use E|O-EO|² in the variance.
statements.required_scope: k1,k2 and O fixed; one bounded mixed trace z in the declared finite action. An eta-dependent O adds a derivative term. A growing sum of mixed terms needs its own size-uniform bound.

statements.statement: At every fixed finite rational triple, exact uncapped Taylor covariance intervals converge to the true finite-measure covariance; if the covariance is nonzero, some finite degree certifies its sign.
statements.argument: For fixed M, R_N tends to0 and N+2>M eventually holds. All four exact polynomial centers converge uniformly in the bounded insertions. Jensen keeps Z>=1, and interval addition, multiplication and positive division are continuous on the resulting bounded intervals. Both covariance endpoints therefore converge to C. Nonzero C leaves an open sign neighborhood eventually containing the complete interval.
statements.required_scope: The formula/oracle is extended to every finite degree and exact arithmetic succeeds at each requested degree. The delivered degree cap48 is separate and makes no eventual-sign guarantee for all parameters. At C=0 the generic sign search need not terminate.

statements.statement: For the same fixed k1,k2 finite family, |Cprime(eta)|<=2 for every finite real eta.
statements.argument: Cprime is the centered third cumulant E[delta x delta y delta z]. Since |delta z|<=2, Cauchy–Schwarz gives |Cprime|<=2 E|delta x delta y|<=2 sqrt(Var x Var y)<=2. This supports exact point-enclosure transport by2 times the maximum distance to the center.
statements.required_scope: A parameter interval still needs exact coverage with no gaps and a positive transported margin in each cell; this derivative theorem alone does not provide a completed cover.
